name: RetinaFace
plain: RetinaFace (ResNet-50, MobileNet-0.25; biubug6 / facexlib): finds faces with a box and five landmarks (eyes, nose, mouth corners); the detector CodeFormer and GFPGAN use for face restoration. MIT.
summary: RetinaFace (Deng et al., CVPR 2020) in the facexlib / Pytorch_Retinaface version: single-stage face detection with five facial landmarks (eyes, nose, mouth corners), the detector of the CodeFormer / GFPGAN face restoration pipelines. A ResNet-50 or MobileNet-0.25 backbone, an FPN, SSH context modules and per-anchor face, box and landmark heads on the stride 8 / 16 / 32 maps. Takes the whole image at its own size (no resize, as facexlib's default `use_origin_size=True`); vendored from facexlib 0.3.0 (no facexlib / torchvision dependency). The portable `module()` maps the image to the raw head maps (anchor decoding and NMS stay outside).

papers.title: RetinaFace: Single-stage Dense Face Localisation in the Wild

official.reason: The authors' MXNet release has no PyTorch weights; facexlib's PyTorch port (from biubug6/Pytorch_Retinaface) is the detector the face restorers use.

limitations: module() exports the raw per-level head maps; anchor decoding and NMS remain outside the exported graph.
No per-landmark confidence: keypoint_scores repeats the face score.
The image is not resized: large photos cost time and memory in proportion to their pixels; downscale them first for big faces.
task_io: Input: one RGB image and a box per person. Output: keypoints with confidence scores for every person.

parity.text: CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 0.001 vs the original. GPU, float16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 0.016 and p99 <= 0.04 (absolute error of the output `keypoints`).
